title: Sunny and the Gumnut Babies | Bedtime Story
description: Sonny the Quokka finds clusters of tiny round gumnuts hanging on a moonlit branch and imagines tiny creatures sleeping inside their snug little wooden homes. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
The branch was covered in gumnuts.

Little round ones, clustered together in groups of three and four — smooth and silver-grey in the moonlight, each one perfectly formed. Some had tiny lids still on. Some were open, their centres dark and hollow.

Sunny reached up and touched one very gently. It was smooth and cool and solid. A tiny wooden ball.

She thought: what if something lives in there?

She looked at the closed ones. The ones with their little lids still on.

She imagined the tiniest creatures curled inside — smaller than her thumbnail — each one cosy in its round wooden home. A little bed made of tree. Safe and dry and just the right size.

Maybe they were sleeping right now.

She moved closer and peered at the nearest gumnut, just to be respectful, in case anything was resting.

The moonlight caught the wood and made it glow a soft silver-grey.

Sunny whispered very quietly to the gumnuts: sleep well, little ones.

Then she moved on a little way down the path and sat against the trunk of the same tree.

The gumnuts hung above her, swaying ever so gently in the breeze.

Sunny watched them sway. Back and forth. Back and forth.

Like little cradles.

And she fell asleep beneath them, dreaming of very small creatures in very cosy wooden beds.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, gumnut babies. Goodnight, little one.
